QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_21

question.text: Bal Vikas Samiti's draft LFM lists the indicator 'Increase literacy rate for project beneficiaries'. Which revision makes it fully SMART?

answer.text: Increase literacy rate among 3,000 project beneficiaries (girls aged 10-14 in 40 villages of Bihar) from baseline 42% to 65% by 31 March 2027, measured by standardised ASER reading assessment
Increase literacy rate as much as possible
Increase literacy rate someday in the future

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 4.2.3, SMART requires Specific (3,000 beneficiaries, girls aged 10-14, 40 villages Bihar), Measurable (42% -> 65%, ASER assessment), Achievable (23-point lift over 2 years is plausible), Relevant (literacy outcome), Time-bound (by 31 March 2027). Option B meets every criterion; the others retain vague language. The Trap: B uses a qualitative adverb ('significantly'). C has no ceiling. D is untimed. All three fail basic SMART tests. Cross-Exam Context: SMART testing repeats across XXIII Ch 4 and Ch 5, and is a staple of education CSR assessment (X-A Investment Adviser, Section 135). Assessor's Pro-Tip: Standardise on a SMART checklist tick-box. Reject any indicator lacking all five ticks. This one-page discipline prevents hours of rework at AIR stage.
